title: Pilot closure scripting and security evidence pocketbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This pocketbook is a compact, tactical reference for Sales Engineers (SEs), Account Executives (AEs), and Solutions Architects running pilot projects that need to be closed to a committed contract. It bundles: conversation scripts for pilot close meetings, an evidence checklist for security/compliance requests, a pricing scaffold for rapid commercial proposals, and a short competitive brief to use when customers question vendor economics or controls.

Who should use this doc
- SEs leading technical demos and handoffs
- AEs driving commercial negotiations and pilot-to-contract closure
- Solutions Architects preparing customer risk responses
- Customer Success for onboarding expectations post-signing

High-level approach
1) Close pilots by removing friction: align acceptance criteria to commercial milestones, deliver a narrow evidence pack to unblock security, and present a pricing anchor that maps to measured pilot metrics.
2) Use the scripts below verbatim where appropriate; adapt tone for customer style.
3) If security requests exceed the evidence pack, escalate using the triage playbook (section: "Security escalation matrix").

1. Pilot close meeting script (30 minutes)
- 0–5 min: Reconnect/Agenda
  - Greeting and meeting purpose: "We want to confirm your acceptance criteria, review pilot telemetry, and get alignment on the contractual next step."
  - State agenda and timebox.
- 5–15 min: Results summary (SE presents)
  - Show 3 KPI slides: latency P95, tokens-per-call cost, functional accuracy vs. gold set. Use the standardized slide template (link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/pilot-slide-templates).
  - Quick demo of where the model succeeded and one controlled failure case and mitigation.
- 15–20 min: Acceptance mapping (AE + customer)
  - Read acceptance criteria aloud and confirm pass/fail per criterion.
  - If any criterion failed, propose a 7-day follow-up remediation plan and commit owner/owner_team.
- 20–27 min: Commercial proposition (AE)
  - Present two options: "Pilot-completion credit" + monthly commit, and "Short-term reserved" (60–90 day) with optional fast-track onboarding. Use the pricing scaffold table below for numbers.
  - Anchor price using measured pilot throughput (average tokens/day × 30) and desired SLO.
- 27–30 min: Close ask and timeline
  - Ask: "Can we agree to sign the MSA + 3-month reservation to convert the pilot by close-of-business next Wednesday?"
  - If yes: confirm PO/contract owner and next steps. If no: schedule next touch and note objections.

2. Pricing scaffold (example numbers — always recalc from pilot telemetry)

- Inputs (these must be filled before meeting):
  - Average daily tokens (pilot): __
  - Peak simultaneous requests per minute: __
  - Target P95 latency: __ ms
  - Pilot duration used for normalization: __ days

- Simple pricing scenarios (example for a mid-market SaaS pilot):
| Option | Commit term | Monthly committed tokens | Effective per-1k-token rate | Typical monthly cost | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Pilot-conversion credit | 3 months | measured_tokens × 30 | $2.40 | $72k | applies a 20% credit on pilot usage month 1; best when customer wants predictable cost |
| Short reserved | 90 days | 50M tokens/month | $1.90 | $95k | lower unit price for reserve; includes 4-hour onboarding SLA |
| Enterprise annual | 12 months | custom | $1.20–$1.60 | depends | includes dedicated pool, SLA, and extended audit evidence |

- How to pick which option to present:
  - If customer is cost-sensitive but willing to commit — show Short reserved.
  - If customer requires isolation or SLAs — show Enterprise annual and highlight Private/Dedicated capabilities.
  - If timeline is short — use Pilot-conversion credit to remove a blocker to signature.

3. Objection handling: economics and controls (scripted replies)
- Objection: "Your per-token cost is higher than Vendor X."
  - Reply: "We model strictly with production telemetry and include operational guarantees. In many cases our unit economics after caching, batching, and prefix KV reuse reduces the per-effective-token cost. We can run an apples-to-apples simulation using your trace for a deterministic comparison — we'll turn that around in 5 business days."
- Objection: "We need SOC2/ISO evidence and a pen test report before moving forward."
  - Reply: "We can provide our SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 scope summary, and the latest pen-test executive summary within 48 hours. For full reports we typically sign an NDA; our security team can also join a 1:1 to walk through specifics."
- Objection: "What if model regressions show up in production?"
  - Reply: "We include evaluation hooks and quality monitoring as part of the onboarding. Our rollouts default to canary + automatic fallback to an earlier verified model if regressions hit configured thresholds. We’ll provide runbooks and a rollback SLA in the SOW."

4. Security evidence pack (minimal set to unblock procurement/security review)
Provide this as a single ZIP to the prospect (link & checklist). Attach only what is requested; over-sharing increases legal load.
- Essential artifacts (deliver within 48 hours):
  - SOC2 Type II summary (PDF)
  - ISO27001 scope and certificate (PDF)
  - SSP (System Security Plan) executive summary (1–2 pages)
  - Penetration test executive summary (redacted)
  - Data flow diagram (text + ASCII diagram) showing what leaves the customer environment and what is encrypted in transit and at rest
  - List of third-party subprocessors and their SOC compliance status
  - KMS/HSM integration details and key rotation policy summary
  - Privacy and data retention one-pager (retention periods, deletion workflow)

- Optional artifacts (if requested):
  - Full SOC2 report (requires NDA)
  - Full pentest report (NDA + redaction request)
  - Architecture diagram for Private deployment (requires RFP-level engagement)

Security escalation matrix
- Level 1 (SE/AE handling): provide the evidence pack above and a 30-minute Q&A with Solutions Security.
- Level 2 (SecOps review): schedule SecOps 60-minute workshop, create a remediation plan, and commit a delivery date for missing controls.
- Level 3 (Legal or Regulated data): require legal and engineering intake; typical lead time 3–6 weeks for on-prem or private deployment agreements.

5. Competitive brief (short, customer-ready)
- Key competitors to frame against: large cloud-hosted LLM APIs, self-hosted inference runtimes with orchestration, and vendor-locked closed-model providers.
- Competitive strengths (how to present):
  - Unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private: "One API, same controls — reduces integration cost and avoids dual support tracks."
  - Production economics levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization guidance that we operationalize; call out expected ~20–40% cost delta vs naive hosted alternatives on production workloads.
  - Rollouts and reliability: automatic fallback and canary policies with model-version pinning — less risk vs single-model endpoints.
- Typical competitor weak points to highlight:
  - Vendor A (cloud-hosted): strong unit price at low volumes but limited isolation and opaque SLAs.
  - Vendor B (self-hosted runtime): good control but high ops and no built-in monitoring or marketplace of verified models.
  - Vendor C (closed-model): quick to start, but limited model customization and unclear data residency.

6. Case study micro-narrative (1 page) — Retail personalization pilot
- Customer: Mid-market e-commerce company (sample name redacted)
- Problem: Product recommendations had 12% CTR; needed personalization that operates across 100ms latency targets for site search.
- Pilot design: 4-week integration, 2M tokens/day, A/B testing on 5% user traffic, custom prompt templates, and local caching of product embeddings.
- Outcome: CTR improved to 18% in pilot cohort, median P95 latency 95ms, estimated breakeven on added GMV by month 2 if scaled. Customer signed a 6-month reserved contract.
- Evidence used in procurement: SOC2 summary, pen-test exec summary, and a short privacy note referencing scoped data retention.

7. Playbook for packaging the evidence ZIP (operational checklist)
- Step 0: Confirm requested artifacts and required delivery timeline from the customer security contact.
- Step 1: Pull the latest template artifacts from /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging and /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence.
- Step 2: Redact as required and produce an evidence index (one-page manifest).
- Step 3: Create a secure sharing link (signed URL or NDA-gated portal) and send with explanatory note.
- Step 4: Offer a 30–60 minute walkthrough with Security; include attendee list from customer.
- Step 5: Log the delivery in the CRM and create a security ticket for follow-up items.

8. Contract language snippets (to include in SOW/MSA)
- Data handling clause (short): "Redwood Inference will process customer data only to provide inference services. Customer owns their data; Redwood will not use customer prompts or outputs to train models unless explicitly agreed in writing."
- Audit access clause (short): "Subject to NDA, Redwood agrees to provide access to audit artifacts (SOC2, pen-test summary) and a SOC2 bridge letter where required for procurement reviews."
- SLA rollback clause: "In the event of a regression impacting model quality beyond the agreed quality thresholds, Redwood will perform a targeted rollback within the committed rollback SLA window (usually 1 hour for Dedicated customers; 24 hours for Hosted customers)."

9. Hand-off checklist on signature (post-signing tasks mapped to owners)
| Task | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---:|
| Create onboarding project in Console and enable telemetry retention | Customer Success | 2 business days |
| Provision reserved capacity / private environment | Eng Private Deployments | 5 business days |
| Kickoff quality-monitoring evals and set regression thresholds | Eng Applied ML | 3 business days |
| Schedule security onboarding and SOC2 deep-dive if requested | Security & Compliance | 5 business days |

10. Appendix: quick resources (links and templates)
- Pilot slide deck template: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/pilot-slide-templates
- Evidence templates: /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence
- Pricing calculator (spreadsheet): /confluence/sales-enablement/pricing-calculators/pilot-to-reserve
- Contract snippets: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/sow-clauses

Document maintenance
- Owner: go-to-market enablement team (primary contact: Asha Patel)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major product change that affects pricing, SLAs, or security posture.

Contact
- For immediate help during a live close: ring the "Pilot-close" Slack channel and @oncall-se. For security evidence escalations: email security-escalations@redwood.example.com and cc the AE.
